acp.app_description: Connect coding agents over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP): Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, opencode and more. Their file reads and writes and terminal commands all go through the FoxOS kernel (scope limits, write locks, audit, human takeover). Official registry: https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json

bot.app_description: One main bot (Fox) plus any number of other bots. Each bot has a name, avatar, role and instructions, a backend (an ACP coding agent or an OpenAI-compatible model), its own conversation and memory, a workspace scope, skills (pstack), connectors, the machines it may control, approval rules, delegation rules, routines and channels. Settings mirror OpenBot field by field. The main bot can delegate to other bots (bot_task_delegate) and the result comes back to the main conversation.

connector.app_description: Connectors: remote MCP servers (HTTP / SSE), local MCP commands and OAuth apps (PKCE, dynamic registration). The catalog matches OpenBot (Parallel, Exa, Firecrawl, Notion, Google Drive), plus GitHub and custom URLs. Tokens live in the local secret store; each bot enables connectors on its own; write tools ask according to the bot's approval rules.

machines.app_description: One bot can control several FoxOS machines and several bots can share one. The controlled host runs foxos machine serve (HTTPS with a self-signed certificate whose fingerprint the controller pins) and trades a one-time pairing code for a token.
